title: Your first Claude Code session
goal: You will open Claude Code in a real project, request a small README change, review its proposed edit, and approve it.
prerequisites: Permission to install or run software on this computer

steps.where: Windows Start menu, in the search result named "Terminal".
steps.why: Claude Code runs through a terminal window.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a Windows Terminal window with a PowerShell prompt ending in >.
hint_levels: Use the Windows search box.
Search for the app named Terminal, not Command Prompt.
Press the Windows key, type Terminal, then press Enter.

steps.where: PowerShell command line in the active Windows Terminal tab.
steps.why: The version command confirms that Claude Code is installed and available.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a Claude Code version number on the next line.
hint_levels: Type the command at the blinking cursor.
The check uses the Claude command followed by two hyphens and version.
Type claude --version and press Enter; if PowerShell says the command is not recognized, install Claude Code before continuing.

steps.action: Change the terminal location to your project folder.
steps.where: PowerShell command line in Windows Terminal.
steps.why: Starting Claude Code here gives it access to the intended project instead of unrelated files.
steps.checkpoint: You should see your project folder's name immediately before the > prompt.
hint_levels: Use the cd command to choose the working folder.
Put the project's full folder path inside quotation marks after cd.
Type cd "C:\full\path\to\your-project" and press Enter.

steps.where: PowerShell command line inside the project folder.
steps.why: This opens an interactive Claude Code session scoped to the project.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the Claude Code interface with an input prompt near the bottom.
hint_levels: Enter the tool's name by itself.
Run the claude command without --version this time.
Type claude and press Enter; follow the displayed browser sign-in instructions if prompted.

steps.action: Confirm that you trust this project folder if Claude Code asks.
steps.where: Claude Code trust prompt in the terminal.
steps.why: Claude Code needs your confirmation before it can inspect and change files in this folder.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the normal Claude Code input prompt instead of the trust question.
hint_levels: Read the choices shown beneath the folder path.
Choose the option that confirms you trust the files in this folder.
Use the arrow keys to highlight "Yes, I trust this folder," then press Enter.

steps.action: Ask Claude to add a "Getting Started" heading and one placeholder setup sentence to README.md without changing anything else.
steps.where: Claude Code input prompt at the bottom of the terminal interface.
steps.why: A narrowly scoped request produces a small edit that is easy to inspect safely.
steps.checkpoint: You should see Claude inspect README.md and propose an edit or request permission to edit it.
hint_levels: Describe the file, the exact addition, and what must remain untouched.
Tell Claude to edit README.md and limit the change to one heading and one sentence.
Type Add a "Getting Started" heading and one placeholder setup sentence to README.md. Do not change anything else. Then press Enter.

steps.action: Review every added and removed line in Claude Code's proposed diff.
steps.where: Permission panel or colored diff displayed in the Claude Code terminal session.
steps.why: The diff shows exactly what will change before you approve it.
steps.checkpoint: You should see only the new Getting Started heading and setup sentence marked as additions, with no unrelated removals.
hint_levels: Focus on the colored lines rather than Claude's summary.
Lines prefixed with + are additions and lines prefixed with - are removals.
Scroll through the permission panel and verify that only README.md has the two requested additions.

steps.where: Choice list at the bottom of Claude Code's edit-permission panel.
steps.why: Approval allows Claude Code to apply the reviewed change to the project file.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a message that README.md was updated and the normal Claude Code prompt returns.
hint_levels: Choose the one-time approval option.
Select the choice labeled "Yes" rather than an option that grants broader ongoing permission.
Use the arrow keys to highlight "Yes," then press Enter.

steps.action: Run "/diff" to inspect the completed change once more.
steps.where: Claude Code input prompt at the bottom of the terminal interface.
steps.why: A final diff confirms that the accepted result matches the request.
steps.checkpoint: You should see README.md listed with the accepted Getting Started additions and no unexpected file changes.
hint_levels: Use Claude Code's slash command for viewing changes.
The command begins with a forward slash and contains the word diff.
Type /diff and press Enter, then inspect the displayed file changes.
